detail.longDescription: Hello HN. Cordium is a FOSS, self-hosted, identity-based, general-purpose sandbox platform built on Kubernetes. The main differentiator here is that Cordium automatically assigns an identity to each sandbox to provide "secretless" secure remote/zero-trust access to resources/infrastructure (e.g. APIs, SSH, databases, k8s, etc.) without having to hold credentials and secrets (e.g. API keys and access tokens, SSH private keys/passwords, database passwords, mTLS private keys, etc.) inside the sandbox. The way it works is that every Cordium sandbox includes an Octelium ZTNA client (see https://github.com/octelium/octelium ) which routes requests from the sandbox to the upstream resources through the Octelium Cluster running on the same underlying Kubernetes cluster over WireGuard tunnels. In the Octelium Cluster, each upstream resource is protected by a corresponding identity-aware proxy that actually holds the upstream credential that injects the credential on-the-fly to the upstream if the downstream (i.e. the Cordium sandbox) is authorized by an Octelium policy. In short, Cordium is basically a sandbox platform with a dual nature: it doesn't just provide isolated execution runtimes but it also provides and identity and access infrastructure to provide secure secretless remote access, identity management, L7-aware access control and visibility for every request originating from within the sandbox. You can use it for various use cases from a personal self-hosted GitHub Codespaces alternative for remote development as well as a scalable sandbox platform for AI agents to access infrastructure without handling them your credentials at scale. You can also use it as an infrastructure layer to build more complex applications such as agent meshes. The main features include declarative management, Templates and prebuilds, persistent, ephemeral and forkable storage via Kubernetes volume snapshots, lifecycle tasks, controls such as linux caps, read-only filesystem and egress control, access and management over web portal/SSH/CLI as well as SDKs in Go/Rust/Python/Typescript. You can learn more about Cordium, its features in detail and how it works, please visit the docs at https://octelium.com/docs/cordium/latest/overview/intro You can also try a live demo for the Cordium web portal at https://demo.octelium.com/cordium and a CLI playground at https://demo.octelium.com/cli
